title: On Recognising the handwriting at the first glance
subtitle: 文化遗产 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文化遗产（人与社会·历史社会与文化·文化传统与习俗）
meta: 主题语境：文化遗产（人与社会·历史社会与文化·文化传统与习俗）　|　核心词汇：recognise　|　正文 356 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 recognise 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1977 the father ① recognised the handwriting at the first glance without complaint, and every neighbour in the house said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three months on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the father ② recognises the handwriting at the first glance with great care without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ recognise the handwriting at the first glance at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ recognised the handwriting at the first glance before — a line in the letter for September 1971 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Recognising the handwriting at the first glance without complaint, the father said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the chair at the far door, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ recognise the old custom of the district with great care, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Recognise the old custom of the district at once and never mention it again.

By 1984 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the letter, and a new neighbour from the next house ⑧ recognises the old custom of the district without complaint every month without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the door, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ recognised the handwriting at the first glance again when nobody else would.

⑩ To recognise the handwriting at the first glance, my mother said in 1989, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the house remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the house forgets, somebody recognises the handwriting at the first glance with great care again and somebody must recognise the handwriting at the first glance without complaint all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 认出（一般过去式 recognised the handwriting at the first glance：1977 年父亲头一回这样做，毫无怨言地）
B. v. 认出（一般现在 recognises the handwriting at the first glance：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 认出（不定式 to recognise the handwriting at the first glance：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 认出（过去完成时 had recognised the handwriting at the first glance：1971 年九月的家书上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 认出（动名词 recognising the handwriting at the first glance 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 承认（recognise the old custom of the district：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去承认承认这一带那套旧习俗）
G. v. 承认（recognise the old custom of the district：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 认出（后段两处：新来的邻居照例 recognises the old custom of the district，而母亲又一次 recognised the handwriting at the first glance）

answers.why: recognise 意为“认出”，1977 年父亲毫无怨言地认出一眼就认出了那种笔迹，那是老屋里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 recognised。
recognise 意为“认出”，自那以后父亲小心翼翼地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 recognises。
recognise 意为“认出”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯认出一眼就认出了那种笔迹”，此处为不定式 to recognise the handwriting at the first glance。
recognise 意为“认出”，家书里 九月 那行字说明早在 1984 年之前就有人认出过，故用过去完成时 had recognised。
recognise 意为“认出”，父亲说“认出一眼就认出了那种笔迹这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 recognising the handwriting at the first glance 作主语。
recognise 意为“承认”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去承认承认这一带那套旧习俗”，should ever 之后用原形 recognise the old custom of the district。
recognise 意为“承认”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻承认承认这一带那套旧习俗（recognise the old custom of the district at once），以后再也不要提起。
recognise 意为“认出”，新来的邻居每个月份都照例承认承认这一带那套旧习俗，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 recognises。
recognise 意为“认出”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次毫无怨言地认出一眼就认出了那种笔迹，用一般过去式 recognised 叙述。
recognise 意为“认出”，结尾那句是母亲 1989 年的话：要认出一眼就认出了那种笔迹，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和老屋记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 recognise 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1977 the father recognised the handwriting at the first glance without complaint, and nobody in the house forgot it.
Even now the father recognises the handwriting at the first glance with great care whenever the house asks.
Recognising the handwriting at the first glance without complaint, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever recognise the old custom of the district with great care, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new neighbour from the next house recognises the old custom of the district without complaint every month, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother recognised the handwriting at the first glance again, and the house remembered that half.
